title: Beyond the 10-Minute Promise: Decoding the Consumer mindset in the Quick Commerce market
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond the 10-Minute Promise: Decoding the Consumer mindset in the Quick Commerce market

affiliations.org_name: Unaffiliated Authors - affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract: Quick commerce (q-commerce) delivers everyday essentials, including groceries and household products, within minutes of an online order. India has emerged as a major market, with Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy Instamart competing on the promise of 10 minute delivery. As ultra-fast fulfilment becomes a category norm rather than a differentiating advantage, understanding why consumers stay, switch, or abandon platforms is critical. This study examines the psychological, functional, and contextual factors shaping consumer stickiness, engagement, and switching behavior among urban consumers in India’s quick commerce market. A mixed-methods design combines qualitative interviews with active users and a quantitative study, providing insights into motivations, friction points, situational cues, and platform-specific perceptions. The findings reveal behavioural heterogeneity and identify three distinct segments: Convenience Seekers, Price-Sensitive Deal Hunters, and Sporadic Selective Shoppers, each driven by different motivations and triggers. As rapid delivery becomes an expectation, sustained platform preference increasingly depends on reliable service, perceived fairness, and psychological reassurance. Platform loyalty is driven primarily by reliability, product availability, and psychological comfort, whereas switching is associated with perceived pricing unfairness, stockouts, and app-related friction. Quick commerce behaviour reflects both functional performance and psychological assurance, with disruptions to either dimension driving platform abandonment. The study contributes to emerging quick commerce literature by shifting attention from ultra-fast delivery to consumer attributes determining platform preference. Its implications emphasise strengthening service reliability, ensuring product availability, maintaining pricing fairness, and reducing delivery and app-related friction, while recognising the evolving hierarchy of consumer priorities as rapid delivery becomes a category expectation.

title: Intersectional Barriers to Social-Ecological Transformation in the Colombian Amazon

detail.title: Intersectional Barriers to Social-Ecological Transformation in the Colombian Amazon

affiliations.org_name: Unaffiliated Authors - affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract: Social-ecological transformations are vital to prevent crises in climate, biodiversity, and justice. Community-led transformations show promise in promoting sustainability and challenging mainstream obstacles. Yet these efforts face material, institutional, epistemic, cultural, and identity barriers linked to factors such as skin color, ethnicity, and gender. Using ethnography, we contribute to understanding these challenges by studying the barriers a group of Afro-descendant artisanal gold miners in the Colombian Amazon face in transitioning to more conservation-aligned livelihoods. Our results show racial discrimination influenced environmental policy, economic incentives, and access to labor and education, while gender disparities kept women out of community decision-making. Stereotypes about miners limited social-ecological participation as institutions, media, and conservation agencies overlooked Afro-descendants’ territorial identity. Lacking legitimacy and funding, artisanal small-scale gold miners rely on mining to exit the sector. More results like ours are needed to deepen our understanding of barriers faced by marginalized communities and promote successful socio-ecological transformations.

detail.abstract: Federal flood mitigation funding in the United States reaches homeowners through a multi-stage application process administered by local governments, but prior studies observe only who receives funding, not who is eligible or who applies. To identify where inequities emerge, we built a parcel-scale dataset linking flood exposure across 78 events from 1996 to 2020 with Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) applications and funding outcomes for 3.14 million residential properties in eastern North Carolina. Of 202,623 flood-exposed properties, about two-thirds are in jurisdictions with at least one HMA application, yet only 5,746 (2.8%) apply, and 3,432 (59.7%) of those are funded. Repeat-flooded properties apply at nearly four times the rate of once-flooded properties (5.6% vs 1.5%) but are funded at similar rates (58.5% vs 62.0%), even though their higher expected avoided losses make them more cost-effective to fund. Funded properties are concentrated in lower-value block groups with lower White and higher Black population shares than the flood-exposed population (Kolmogorov–Smirnov D = 0.13 and 0.15, p < 0.001), a shift concentrated in buyouts. Within block groups, however, funded properties sit near the local median property value, indicating that value-based selection operates between neighborhoods rather than within them. The application stage is the largest leverage point, so expanding cost-effective mitigation requires raising application rates among repeat-flooded households and the share of their applications that are funded.

title: Identifying bedding-dependent Mode III fracture laws in sandstone using physics-informed neural networks
affiliations: Beijing Jiaotong University and Beijing Jiaotong University

detail.title: Identifying bedding-dependent Mode III fracture laws in sandstone using physics-informed neural networks
detail.abstract: Surface measurements provide indirect information about the internal slip and traction governing Mode III fracture in layered sandstone. We develop a condensed-interface physics-informed neural network (PINN) to jointly identify internal slip fields and cohesive laws from specimen loads and surface displacement increments. Fixed three-dimensional elastic operators couple the learned interface fields to equilibrium and observations. Networks for different notch depths share a constitutive law at each bedding orientation, while work control and a tangent-based critical condition connect the inferred fields to peak capacity. Tests on 27 sandstone discs provide 18 specimens for identification and nine for replicate assessment. Mean absolute relative peak-load errors are 8.03, 6.84 and 2.72% at 0°, 45° and 90°. At 45° and 90°, near-peak traction extends across most of the ligament, with fitted peak strengths of 7.34 and 14.39 MPa, respectively. These results link the higher bedding-perpendicular capacity to greater local strength and explain notch-depth effects through the load-bearing ligament area.

detail.abstract: Multiscale cavitating flows involve the coexistence and strong interaction of large-scale vapor cavities and small-scale discrete bubbles. Although two-way coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian methods provide a viable framework for resolving such multiscale structures, predictive accuracy remains highly sensitive to empirical coefficients that govern bubble nucleation, growth, condensation, and the criterion for scale conversion between Eulerian and Lagrangian descriptions. To address this parametric uncertainty, an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) based data assimilation framework is developed to calibrate four key parameters of a multiscale cavitation model for cavitating flow over a NACA66 hydrofoil. A prior ensemble of thirty parameter combinations is generated via Latin hypercube sampling, and bubble size distributions measured by digital inline holography are assimilated to update the model parameters sequentially. The optimized parameter set, comprising a nucleation-pressure coefficient of 1.4, a growth coefficient of 0.0075, a condensation coefficient of 0.0031, and a critical vapor volume fraction threshold of 0.65 for Eulerian–Lagrangian conversion, markedly improves the quantitative representation of the mesoscale bubble population. The total variation measure is reduced from 1.215 to 0.1351, the root-mean-square error from 0.374 to 0.00373, and the coefficient of determination increases from 0.2112 to 0.9925. Without further recalibration, the optimized model also exhibits strong predictive capability under different cavitation numbers, yielding close agreement with experimental data for both shock wave driven cloud cavitation and sheet cavitation regimes. These results demonstrate that EnKF-based calibration not only substantially enhances the prediction of mesoscale bubble statistics but also preserves accurate macroscale cavity dynamics across distinct cavitation regimes, thereby offering a more robust numerical tool for multiscale cavitation investigations.

title: Existence of a majority equilibrium in the presence of a reference point
affiliations: New York University Abu Dhabi and University of Sheffield

detail.title: Existence of a majority equilibrium in the presence of a reference point
detail.abstract: We study the existence of majority equilibria in multidimensional policy spaces when choices are made in the presence of a reference point, for example an incumbent. Voters are described by strict preference correspondences such that, for any incumbent policy, the set of strictly preferred alternatives is contained in a pointed cone with vertex at that policy. Theorem 1 shows that a majority equilibrium exists whenever the cone angle is smaller than $\arcsin\sqrt{(d{+}1)/(2d)}$ with a dimension-free bound at $45^\circ$. In a Euclidean model with ideal points, Theorem 3 shows that for random electorates in high dimensions, majority equilibria exist with probability one even when the angle is close to $90^\circ$, the unrestricted case.

title: The Moderating Role of Emissions Trading in the Carbon Reduction Effect of Green Finance: Evidence from Guangzhou City of China
affiliations: Nanjing Normal University and Beijing Normal University

detail.title: The Moderating Role of Emissions Trading in the Carbon Reduction Effect of Green Finance: Evidence from Guangzhou City of China

keywords: Green Finance Reform and Innovation Pilot Zone

detail.abstract: China's pilot zones for green finance reform and innovation (PZGFRI) represent a major institutional experiment aimed at channeling financial resources toward low-carbon development. Whether PZGFRI can generate persistent and observable carbon emissions reduction remains empirically unsettled. This study analyses Guangzhou PZGFRI using a panel of prefecture-level cities of China over 1993–-2022, and employs synthetic difference-in-differences to conduct case-oriented policy evaluations. The findings are as follows. First, the Guangzhou pilot significantly reduced carbon emissions, with the effect emerging after a lag and accumulating over time. Second, China’s regional emissions trading scheme (ETS) positively moderates this reduction effect. Third, mechanism tests indicate two channels under ETS constraints: green technological innovation and low-carbon industrial restructuring. A placebo test using biogenic carbon emissions yields no significant effect, supporting the specificity of the proposed mechanisms. Overall, this study demonstrates that the carbon reduction effect of Guangzhou PZGFRI is conditional on ETS constraints, indicating that emissions trading constitutes a key institutional condition for enhancing the environmental effectiveness of green finance. It enriches the theoretical framework and empirical evidence for the precise assessment of green finance policy effects, providing practical implications for green finance institutional design and advancing regional low carbon transitions through green finance instruments.

detail.abstract: We study random assignment of indivisible objects among a set of agents with strictpreferences and outside options. When agents may rank some objects as unacceptable,we consider different notions of measuring waste of object(s) from an ex-ante perspective.The most natural one is q-agent-object-waste whereby both one agent and oneof his acceptable objects are unassigned with at least probability q. On the one hand,we show that any mechanism satisfying equal treatment of almost equals (wherebyany two agents with identical rankings over objects receive the same probability sharesfor objects they both regard acceptable), strategy-proofness and ex-post weak nonwastefulness(whereby in any assignment in the support we cannot have that both oneagent and one of his acceptable objects are unassigned) must be q-agent-object-wastefulwith q ≥ 1/6 . We show that random serial dictatorship (RSD) attainsthe minimal bound of 1/6 in this class for four agents or three objects. In addition, weconsider q-object-wastefulness where an object remains unassigned with probability q,while agents, who consider it acceptable, remain unassigned with aggregate probabilityq. RSD attains the minimal bound of 1/4 in this class of mechanismswith respect to q-object-wastefulness for three objects.

title: Exchange-Rate Volatility, Financial Development, and Economic Growth: Panel Evidence from Emerging Asian Economies
affiliations: Wuhan University

detail.title: Exchange-Rate Volatility, Financial Development, and Economic Growth: Panel Evidence from Emerging Asian Economies
detail.abstract: It is this paper that discusses the effect of ERV and FD on the economic growth of eight emerging Asian economies for the period of 2000–2025. Using a balanced panel of 208 country-year observations, we estimate pooled OLS, two-way fixed effects, random effects, and system generalized method of moments (GMM) specifications, as well as second generation panel cointegration, Dumitrescu–Hurlin causality, and panel vector autoregression (PVAR) analyses.,The data suggest that the impact on real GDP growth is statistically significant and economically significant negative when the financial development index is less than about 0.55, but these negative effects are dampened significantly when financial development levels are higher. The marginal effect of a one-standard-deviation shock to ERV ranges from –1.03 percentage points in the least financially developed sub-sample to –0.19 percentage points in the most financially developed sub-sample. The results are stable across different measures of volatility, across sub-samples, common correlated effects estimation, and across exclusion of years of the global financial crisis and the COVID-19 years.,The paper highlights the complementarities of exchange-rate management and financial deepening in the architecture of macro-financial stability frameworks in emerging Asia.

detail.abstract: Abstract: Forward and inverse rehearsals, conducted in flood-defense applications of digital-twin watersheds, respectively require high-fidelity and rapid simulations of river corridor flood dynamics based on hydrodynamic model (HDM). In this study, two key techniques are proposed to improve these rehearsals. First, Technique-1 is proposed for 2D HDM to couple the terrain time series of newly-defined ribbon-like objects, to automatically regulate regional connectivity in flood simulation. It yields an enhanced 2D model capable of performing high-fidelity simulation of river corridor flood dynamics under complex spatiotemporal variations in regional connectivity, for the forward rehearsal. Second, Technique-2 is proposed to combine 1D HDM and fine 2D grid, involving a seed-spread method to interpolate cross-sectional hydrological data onto 2D grid, and a guided-search algorithm for creating newly-defined subdomain-based inundation units. It turns a 1D HDM into a composite model capable of synchronously simulating flood-routing and inundation distributions in a large river system and its adjacent land, for the inverse rehearsal. These new models are tested using a real levee-breach flood, the annual flood in a large river-lake system, as well as the Li River corridor (including urban area with complex building layouts). The enhanced model is further demonstrated by a comparison study using Mike21, while the composite model is shown to run in second-level real-time in the tests of watershed-scale simulations and be two orders of magnitude faster than a 2D HDM. The new models improve systematically the multi-level integrated simulations of river corridor flood dynamics for digital-twin watersheds, and will provide fundamental tools and new perspectives for agent-invoked automatic flood simulations in the AI era.

title: Multilevel spillover effect among crypto assets, gold, developed and emerging equities: A time-frequency analysis with block aggregation
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics and Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

affiliations.org_name: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

detail.abstract: Understanding return spillovers between digital assets and traditional finance requires distinguishing market groups. This study investigates the time-frequency risk spillovers and driving macroeconomic factors among cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, gold, developed and emerging equities from Jan. 2019 to Jan. 2026. A framework is proposed by combining TVP-VAR model, Diebold--Yilmaz spillover measure, Baruník--Křehlík frequency decompositions (TVP-VAR-DY-BK), and block-aggregated network analysis, to preserves constituent-level information and separate within-block from cross-block spillovers. The results show that cross-block connectedness is predominantly short-term. Developed equities are the principal net transmitters, while emerging equities, stablecoins, and gold are net recipients on average. Cryptocurrencies generally receive short-term net spillovers from developed equities, while transmitting net spillovers to emerging equities across frequency bands. Stablecoins mainly receive short-term net spillovers with brief reversals around the USDC depeg. Macroeconomic associations vary across horizons and aggregation levels. These findings highlight the value of distinguishing market groups and internal from external connections for risk monitoring and the assessment of cross-asset portfolio exposures.

title: Critical Minerals Mining and County-Level Economic Outcomes in the United States: A Fixed-Effects Panel Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Cape Coast

detail.title: Critical Minerals Mining and County-Level Economic Outcomes in the United States: A Fixed-Effects Panel Analysis

affiliations.org_name: Unaffiliated Authors - affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract: The March 2025 executive order "Immediate Measures to Increase American Mineral Production" named uranium, copper, potash, and gold as minerals of national-security importance, but whether US counties that host these minerals show different economic outcomes from otherwise-similar counties has not been tested in a systematic, recent, national panel. Using a county-level panel of 3,213 US counties, 2006–2025, built from USGS mineral-site records and Bureau of Labor Statistics county employment, unemployment, and wage data, this study tests whether hosting a Producer or Past-Producer critical-mineral site predicts three economic outcomes: unemployment rate, employment level, and average weekly wage. Because mining-site presence is a historically fixed county attribute rather than a variable that changes year to year, county fixed effects are not identified for this treatment; the study instead compares naive pooled estimates against a within-state, common-year specification (state and year fixed effects), the valid analogue for a time-invariant regressor. Naive comparisons show every mineral associated with higher wages; none of these wage premiums survive state-and-year fixed effects. Naive unemployment-rate associations for copper and gold counties also do not survive. Two findings do survive: gold-mining counties and, more broadly, counties with any critical-mineral site have systematically larger employment bases even within their own state a result that holds even after controlling for county land area, which we show is itself significantly larger in treated counties and so a plausible mechanical confound, and uranium-mining counties show significantly higher unemployment than other counties in the same state as a result invisible in the naive comparison that survives a full leave-one-state-out check across all 22 states with uranium sites and a Bonferroni correction within the unemployment-rate outcome family, though not a stricter correction across all fifteen state-and-year fixed-effects tests reported. Two supplementary machine-learning checks corroborate both surviving results: a double machine-learning estimation that replaces the linear land-area control with a flexible gradient-boosted model leaves both coefficients intact and, if anything, slightly larger, while a regularized-regression prediction exercise, evaluated on counties held out entirely from fitting, independently ranks uranium and gold as the strongest predictors of their respective outcomes. We interpret this pattern using the resource-curse and boom-bust literature: most naive mining-county correlations reflect which states have mining, not mining's local effect, while the uranium result is consistent with the well-documented post-boom economic legacy of Cold War-era uranium districts.

detail.abstract: Global water pollution requires the rapid development of efficient photocatalysts for wastewater remediation, yet traditional trial-and-error approaches are time-consuming and cannot effectively reveal complex multivariate reaction systems. In this study, we first synthesized and evaluated a series of single- and co-doped (B/Tb) BiOBr photocatalysts. The optimal 0.5% B-1% Tb co-doped BiOBr exhibited superior activity, achieving 99.35% degradation of Rhodamine B within 60 min. We then combined our experimental results with literature data to construct a comprehensive dataset of 816 entries across 8 variables, establishing a data-driven machine learning (ML) framework. Among ten evaluated algorithms, the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) model achieved the highest predictive accuracy, yielding an R2 of 0.8882 and an RMSE of 0.0894 after Bayesian hyperparameter optimization. Feature importance and SHAP analyses revealed that reaction time, primary dopant ratio, and solution pH dominate the photocatalytic degradation process. Furthermore, to validate the generalization capability of the model, we synthesized two novel unexplored systems (B/Ce-BOB and Tb/S-BOB), demonstrating excellent agreement between the predicted and actual experimental degradation efficiencies. Overall, this integrated experimental and ML-guided workflow significantly accelerates the rational design, prediction, and optimization of advanced photocatalytic materials.

detail.abstract: Machine learning models often achieve high predictive accuracy for alloy properties under random splits, but this does not guarantee reliable deployment when data are heterogeneous and unevenly distributed. Accuracy alone, however, does not indicate whether the supporting evidence is sufficient. We therefore formulate alloy-state screening as an evidence-gated decision problem rather than a regression task alone. The method uses two branches, one for multi-property prediction and one for evidence-support evaluation, and combines them into action labels through a reliability gate. Here, evidence support is characterized by source reliability, feature coverage, out of distribution distance, and physical consistency (based on the Wiedemann–Franz relation), so that predictive accuracy and evidential support are assessed separately. Furthermore, using over 8,000 aluminium records and evidence‐aware views, the framework distinguishes interpolation capacity from deployable performance. Across source splits, family holdouts, and external benchmarks, internal interpolation overestimates deployment reliability, while the gate identifies predictions with insufficient evidence support that are unsuitable for direct use. The central question is therefore not only how accurate a prediction is, but whether it is sufficiently supported for engineering use.

title: Modeling User-News Relations for Fake News Detection via a Multi-view Collaborative Filtering Network

detail.title: Modeling User-News Relations for Fake News Detection via a Multi-view Collaborative Filtering Network

affiliations.org_name: Unaffiliated Authors - affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract: Fake news detection on social media is critical for maintaining the health and security of the cyberspace ecosystem. Existing user-modeling methods exploit social connections and static profile attributes to identify rumors, yet malicious actors (e.g., social bots) can easily forge these attributes, leading to inaccurate user modeling and degraded detection performance. We use observed user-news interaction behaviors as complementary evidence for user modeling. To this end, we propose a **Multi-view Collaborative Filtering Network (MCFN)**, which models user-news behavioral relationships across different news-label classes. MCFN constructs a class-wise interaction matrix and propagates information between users and news across multiple label-specific views, capturing dynamic behavioral patterns that distinguish genuine from malicious participants. Contrastive learning aligns global news representations sharing the same label to sharpen the decision boundary between fake and real news. To handle users with sparse interaction histories, we employ meta-learning to rapidly infer per-user label-preference weights, supporting adaptation under low-resource conditions. Additionally, the dispersion of cross-view similarity scores is used to quantify preference explicitness, assigning larger weights to users whose behavioral representations exhibit stronger label-specific discriminability. Experiments on three real-world benchmarks (Twitter15, Twitter16, and Weibo16) demonstrate that MCFN achieves strong performance in both standard and early fake news detection settings.

title: Finding the Block: Costly Coalition Search and Persistence Outside the Core

detail.abstract: I study costly search for blocking coalitions in transferable-utility games. In an explicit family of monotone, superadditive games, the ordinary core is empty in every realized state and a maximum blocker raises its members' aggregate payoff by one eighth. Nevertheless, if 𝑝 𝑛 is the best one-query probability of finding any blocking certificate, every adaptive policy using at most 𝑄 value queries succeeds with probability at most 𝑄 𝑝 𝑛 , where 𝑝 𝑛 ∼ 3-1/2 2-0.540852𝑛. Conditional on finding any blocker, at most 𝑛 additional queries recover a maximum-gain blocker. This exponential-first-discovery/linear-refinement asymmetry yields matching bounds on discoverable blocking surplus and an asymptotically sharp threshold for profitable search entry: every fixed positive query price eventually deters search despite an empty core. The construction extends to any fixed number of at least three hidden groups, and the refinement argument applies to a broader class of upward-closed productive sets. A mandatory-first-block rule lowers the entry threshold by a factor of order 𝑛. The results quantify when core instability exists but is not worth discovering.

detail.abstract:
This study examined the effect of trade diversification on Nigeria’s dependence on crude oil export revenues from 1990 to 2024. It assessed the impact of non-oil exports on Nigeria’s dependence on crude oil export revenues, and examined the effect of exchange rate movements on Nigeria’s dependence on crude oil export revenues. 

The study was anchored on the Dutch Disease Theory and adopted an ex post facto research design using annual secondary data obtained from relevant national and international statistical sources. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) technique was employed alongside descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, unit root tests, bounds testing, diagnostic tests, and stability tests. The unit root results showed that the variables were stationary after first differencing, while the bounds test indicated no evidence of cointegration in the main oil export dependence model but evidence of a long-run relationship between exchange rate and trade diversification at the 10 percent significance level. 

The empirical findings revealed that trade diversification had a statistically significant effect on oil export dependence, while non-oil exports had no statistically significant effect. Exchange rate movements were also found to have a significant negative long-run effect on trade diversification. 

The study concludes that reducing Nigeria’s dependence on crude oil requires a broader and more competitive export structure rather than merely increasing the nominal value of non-oil exports. It recommends sustained investment in export-oriented agriculture, manufacturing, solid minerals and value-added industries, alongside improved infrastructure, greater access to export finance, and a more stable and predictable exchange rate environment.

detail.abstract: The law governing UK alternative investment fund managers is expected to change in 2028. HM Treasury is currently consulting on draft legislation to replace the existing EU-derived statutory regime with a domestic framework combining legislation, Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) rules and new fund reporting. Current law expressly requires the FCA to take three steps: use leverage information to identify specified risks, assess leverage risk, and act when intervention becomes necessary. The draft replacement Regulations do not reproduce this three-step chain. The proposed regime introduces a broader duty to use specified information while preserving intervention powers within an architecture that already includes FCA objectives and Financial Policy Committee (FPC) oversight. Better data and greater regulatory flexibility may preserve substantial supervisory capacity, but the legal allocation of responsibility changes. The final framework should identify where each of the three present functions will sit.

detail.abstract: The architecture of modern global capitalism is inextricably bound to the social construction of gender, creating a systemic interdependency between the formal economic sphere of production and the informal, often invisible sphere of social reproduction. While patriarchal social structures predate the capitalist mode of production, the advent of capitalism fundamentally reconfigured gender relations. It enforced a rigid spatial, legal, and conceptual division between commodity production-the market, where waged labor generates surplus value-and social reproduction-the home and community, where unwaged labor sustains and replenishes the human workforce. This bifurcation generated a systemic devaluation of the reproductive and caregiving labor traditionally assigned to women. In contemporary macroeconomic accounting, this work is largely relegated to the invisible background, despite the formal economy's absolute reliance on it to maintain a functional wage-labor force. Consequently, the modern capitalist economic system operates upon a foundational paradox. On one hand, it extracts immense value from female labor-both paid and unpaid-while simultaneously leveraging historical gender norms to structurally marginalize women within the very markets they help sustain. Examining the gendered impact of capitalist structures requires a deeply nuanced, comprehensive analysis of how economic systems shape, reinforce, and occasionally transform the lived experiences of women. The intersection of capitalism and gender inequality manifests persistently across multiple, overlapping domains. These include the exhausting "double burden" of unpaid domestic labor, severe market stratification, and deeply entrenched horizontal and vertical occupational segregation 1. Furthermore, the capitalist paradigm presents a profound dialectical tension for women across the globe. The wage-labor market offers an unprecedented avenue for financial autonomy, individual actualization, and emancipation from traditional patriarchal dependency. Yet, it simultaneously incorporates women into a highly exploitative corporate nexus that capitalizes on their historical marginalization, often utilizing them as a flexible, underpaid reserve army of labor 1. To unravel these immense complexities, this comprehensive report employs a multidisciplinary approach, drawing heavily upon Marxist feminism, Social Reproduction Theory (SRT), and institutional economics. By grounding theoretical insights in robust empirical evidence-ranging from International Labour Organization (ILO) statistics on unpaid care work to the World Economic Forum's (WEF) Global Gender Gap metrics-the analysis illuminates the precise structural mechanics of gender inequality 4. Ultimately, evaluating the systemic and intersectional nature of these disparities sets the stage for a rigorous policy analysis. This report wi l determine whether interventions such as universal state-sponsored childcare, legislative pay transparency mandates, and cooperative business models can meaningfuly disrupt the gendered exploitation inherent in contemporary capitalism.

detail.abstract: This study examines the initial ex-post behavioural and fiscal effects of the introduction of the Global Minimum Tax (GMT), focusing on the Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax in a high-tax jurisdiction. We use a panel micro-dataset of 2,300 MNE subgroups located in Italy, covering fiscal years 2018–2024, and apply the Synthetic Difference-in-Differences methodology. Although all subgroups in our dataset are potentially affected by the reform, as they belong to multinational groups with global revenues exceeding 750 million euros, the treated subgroups are identified as those with an effective tax rate below 15% in at least two pre-reform years (10% of the sample analysed). Results indicate that, following the reform’s announcement and implementation, treated subgroups significantly increased their CIT payments compared with their synthetic counterfactual. In our preferred specification, the effect is particularly pronounced in the holding and financial sectors, where CIT payments of the treated are approximately five times the counterfactual level, while in other sectors treated subgroups’ payments doubled. These findings suggest that the reform might have prompted spontaneous compliance among multinationals by aligning CIT effective tax rates with the new minimum, generating positive fiscal outcomes even before the first scheduled payments of the domestic minimum tax. This result is compatible with MNEs’ willingness to prevent reputational risks as part of their Corporate Social Responsibility commitments.

detail.abstract: Cross-border digital payments are increasingly important to trade, remittances, financial inclusion, and economic integration across the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS). Despite rapid growth in digital financial services, transactions across national borders can remain costly, slow, fragmented, and vulnerable to failure because payment systems, financial institutions, currencies, regulatory requirements, and technical infrastructures differ between countries. Interoperable payment systems provide an opportunity to reduce these barriers by enabling different financial networks and payment providers to communicate and process transactions across institutional and national boundaries. This article examines the relationship between payment interoperability and cross-border transaction efficiency across ECOWAS. detail.abstract: Reliable characterization of gamma-emitting radionuclides in radioactive-waste drums is complicated by unknown source location, attenuation, and the trade-off between measurement time and information content. This study presents an information-guided adaptive Bayesian framework that couples OpenMC-derived detector responses with sequential Bayesian inference to select each new detector angle from the evolving posterior distribution. A 200-L steel drum containing a homogeneous polyethylene-equivalent matrix was modeled in OpenMC with a narrow-collimated ORTEC GEM50-83 HPGe detector. A Monte Carlo full-energy-peak-efficiency (FEPE) response library was refined in radius and relative angle and interpolated onto 545 candidate source positions in the drum cross-section. The Bayesian model jointly inferred 2D source position and ¹³⁷Cs activity, while expected information gain selected among eight candidate views. A 15% multiplicative response-model uncertainty was represented by a negative-binomial likelihood, and acquisition stopped when posterior spatial RMS uncertainty was ≤3 cm and activity coefficient of variation was ≤20%. After model freezing, four previously unseen source positions and four activities (25–250 kBq) were evaluated in 480 stochastic trials. Mean and median localization errors were 1.65 and 1.17 cm, respectively; 90.2% and 94.0% of trials were within 3 and 5 cm. Activity mean absolute percentage error was 19.2%, the joint stopping rule was met in 78.1% of trials, and the mean number of detector positions was 5.71 rather than eight, a 28.6% reduction. These results support the computational feasibility of adaptive, uncertainty-aware spatial characterization, while showing that quantitative activity estimation remains more sensitive to residual response-model mismatch and requires experimental validation.

detail.abstract: Saline groundwater and high evaporative demand constrain forage production in hyper-arid drylands, yet suitable water-management strategies remain poorly defined. We combined two years of multi-cut barley field experiments in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, with APSIM Next Generation simulations to assess production limits and water-salinity management. Seasonal dry biomass at 2000 ppm reached 9.73 and 7.91 t ha⁻¹; losses were 8 and 29% at 6000 ppm and 25 and 45% at 10000 ppm, with no significant genotype × salinity interaction. Irrigation at 50% ETc nearly doubled irrigation-water productivity (14.5 versus 7.8 kg ha⁻¹ mm⁻¹). APSIM reproduced biomass and regrowth well (calibration R² = 0.90, RMSE = 85 g m⁻²; evaluation R² = 0.61, RMSE = 172 g m⁻²). Simulations across 181 farms estimated potential yield near 14 t ha⁻¹ season⁻¹. Attainable yield remained close to potential below about 20 dS m⁻¹ root-zone salinity but declined rapidly above this level. Water productivity was highest at 60–80% reference evapotranspiration, about 25% higher than full irrigation. Combining deficit irrigation, nitrogen management, sowing date and genotype increased yield from 1.9 to 13.9 t ha⁻¹ using 20% less irrigation water and reduced between-season variability from 98 to 6%. Forage barley can therefore be produced with saline groundwater when root-zone salinity is controlled and irrigation, leaching and nitrogen are managed together.

detail.abstract: Cloud service subscribers (CSS) face persistent security challenges arising from shared responsibility models, limited infrastructure visibility, multi-tenancy, and evolving cyber threats. Existing standards and frameworks, including ISO/IEC 27017, ISO/IEC 27036, Cloud Security Alliance guidance, and NIST recommendations, provide comprehensive security controls; however, they are largely provider-oriented, fragmented, and insufficiently structured to support subscriber-side decision-making across the cloud subscription lifecycle. This study proposes a lifecycle-aware risk-based cloud security framework designed specifically for CSS. The framework maps cloud security risks to ISO-aligned controls across three subscription phases (pre-subscription, during-subscription, and post-subscription) and integrates cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS), risk categorization mechanisms, and decision-support algorithms into a unified operational model. It was developed using a Design Science Research methodology that combined systematic analysis of international standards, cloud security literature, and industry practice with expert-oriented validation. A formal model links lifecycle stages, service models, risk categories, and controls, while a residual-risk-based decision mechanism recommends mitigation, transfer, acceptance, avoidance, or expert-review actions. More than 40 controls derived from ISO/IEC 27017, ISO/IEC 27036, and ISO/IEC 27002 are consolidated into a traceable lifecycle-oriented mapping structure. Validation using 66 attack scenarios drawn from the CICIDS2017 and TON_IoT datasets yielded a risk coverage ratio of 92.4%, a control mapping coverage of 89.1%, decision completeness of 100%, a traceability score of 90.3%, and an estimated residual risk reduction of 71.6%. The framework operationalizes international security standards into a subscriber-centric model that improves risk-control traceability and supports more secure cloud adoption.

detail.abstract: This paper presents GeoDeep-NURBS, a geometry-aware framework for freeform surface reconstruction integrating positive-weight rational NURBS fitting, learned local refinement, and validation-guided adaptive representation selection. A 12-input neural policy is used for bounded control-point updates, while deterministic objective-based acceptance helps achieve stable optimization. Curvature and density variants assess the importance of geometric features. GeoDeep-NURBS is studied through 6,048 primary synthetic fits, 360 adaptive synthetic fits, and 480 range-scan fits on two Stanford geometries, using multiple observation and training seeds with bootstrap-based uncertainty evaluation. Learned refinement gives accuracy comparable to gain-ranked refinement, while ablation results support the contribution of curvature information. Validation-guided representation adaptation pro-vides the largest gain, reducing mean RMSE by 15.23% in the controlled synthetic experiment and 9.9% on the Stanford Bunny patch while selecting compact control representations. Evaluation on the Stanford Drill patch further shows that the preferred representation is geometry dependent. Overall, GeoDeep-NURBS provides an interpretable framework combining explicit NURBS geometry, guarded learned scheduling, and adaptive representation selection for sparse freeform surface reconstruction while retaining editabilityfor subsequent CAD-oriented geometric processing applications

detail.abstract: This study investigates whether fixed-split performance measures are sufficient for assessing the reliability of sentiment classification models under temporal shift. We compare two frozen prompted local LLMs, qwen2.5:3b-instruct and phi3.5:latest, with two task-adapted supervised baselines, TF--IDF Logistic Regression and DistilBERT, using temporally partitioned Climate and Yelp sentiment datasets. The evaluation covers three class-balanced temporal settings: Climate-500, Yelp-500, and Yelp-1000. Each setting contains train, within-period, short-distance, and long-distance slices; the train slice is used for task-adapted baselines, while the within-period, short-distance, and long-distance slices are used for evaluation. Climate-500 and Yelp-500 contain 1,000 examples per sampled split, and Yelp-1000 contains 2,000 examples per sampled split, repeated across five paired seeds. Models are evaluated using predictive performance, temporal robustness, calibration, prompt sensitivity, selective prediction, latency, structured-output consistency, and temporal-forensics measures. Results show that task adaptation is most beneficial on Climate: DistilBERT achieves 0.8049 Macro-F1, compared with 0.6105 for the strongest frozen prompted LLM, but still drops by 0.0552 and 0.0568 Macro-F1 on the short- and long-distance targets. On Yelp, frozen prompted LLMs perform best, with Qwen reaching 0.9616 and 0.9601 Macro-F1 in Yelp-500 and Yelp-1000. However, reliability differences emerge beyond Macro-F1: in Yelp-1000, Phi shows lower prompt sensitivity than Qwen (0.0056 vs. 0.0623) and lower covered risk under selective prediction (0.0436 vs. 0.0861). Temporal forensics further show stronger lexical novelty and distributional movement in Climate than Yelp, helping explain the different temporal reliability patterns. These findings indicate that sentiment model trust should be assessed through multidimensional reliability profiles rather than headline accuracy.

detail.abstract: When higher-level governments require local governments to implement and finance targeted tax cuts, local governments may offset the resulting revenue losses by increasing non-targeted levies, weakening the intended policy effects. We study how local governments rebalance their budgets and distribute the resulting fiscal costs across firms, using China's expansion of corporate income tax (CIT) reductions for small firms. Exploiting cross-city variation in CIT revenue losses, we find that higher city-level non-tax revenue largely offset lower CIT revenue, leaving total fiscal revenue unchanged. Other tax revenues and public expenditures changed little. Firm-level evidence shows that fees and charges increased for both beneficiary and non-beneficiary firms, while other tax-related burdens did not change significantly. For beneficiary firms, the average increase in fees payable offset 91.6% of their CIT savings, and greater city-level tax-cut intensity did not significantly improve firm performance. For non-beneficiary large firms, fees increased without any offsetting tax relief, and profitability declined in cities with greater tax-cut intensity, implying that using these firms as controls can overstate the estimated effects of the tax cut. These results show why local fiscal rebalancing matters for evaluating the incidence and effectiveness of targeted tax cuts.​

Stronger fiscal expansion and greater financial persistence lower this threshold. Even below it, fiscal influence raises the stationary variance of financial imbalances, connecting regulatory governance to risk amplification. A committed debt-triggered prudential floor can preserve contraction under admissible policy bounds.

detail.abstract: How much should colleges reward academic work that students complete before they arrive on campus? As students increasingly enter college with credit earned through programs such as Advanced Placement, colleges must decide how much of this work should count toward a degree. College credit policies can reduce the time and cost of completing college, but may also allow students to bypass coursework without fully mastering its material. This paper evaluates a statewide AP credit policy reform in Texas that expanded eligibility for AP credit at public institutions. Using a difference-in-differences design, I estimate the reform’s effects on student outcomes including credit progression, graduation, and labor market entry. The policy increased the share of students satisfying freshman credit requirements before their second semester by four percentage points and raised on-time graduation by three percentage points, with larger gains among men and lower-income students. I also find suggestive evidence that the increase in on-time graduation led to earlier labor market entry. Scaling these estimates to students likely to have been directly affected by the reform yields larger effects on these outcomes. A complementary dosage analysis finds that granting credit for one additional AP exam increased on-time graduation by 0.6–1.4 percentage points among affected students. Overall, the effects on on-time graduation have implications for public spending, as earlier degree completion may reduce the public resources required per degree. The larger graduation effects among lower-income students also suggest that such policies may narrow socioeconomic disparities in college completion.

detail.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) have become dominant paradigms for traffic signal control (TSC). Scaling from isolated intersections to urban networks transforms TSC into a cooperative MARL problem with distinct challenges and methods. However, the absence of a systematic MARL framework in existing surveys has fragmented the literature, making it difficult to trace methodological lineages, compare algorithmic trade-offs, or identify coherent research trajectories. At the same time, despite the empirical success of DRL in simulators, it has not led to equally widespread deployment in real-world scenarios. In response, this paper delivers an analysis that synthesizes general MARL methodology into a systematic framework for network-level coordination, while rigorously examining the TSC-specific sim-to-real gap spanning infrastructure, traffic dynamics, topology, safety, computational constraints, and evaluation practice. Finally, we diagnose prevailing benchmarking blind spots and propose a forward-looking research agenda. Readers can use this survey to understand how seemingly diverse DRL-based TSC methods relate to core MARL mechanisms such as independent learning, CTDE, value factorization, communication, and serialized joint optimization. The survey also gives readers a deployment-oriented boundary of DRL-based TSC methods, clarifying which assumptions, interfaces, and operational constraints shape their practical applicability beyond simulation. It further helps identify future directions, including more deployment-aware benchmarks, algorithms designed for operational constraints, and more systematic adaptation of general MARL advances to TSC.

detail.abstract: The replication crisis has motivated stricter significance thresholds despite limited theoretical justification. A conventional p-value counts outcomes more extreme than those observed. It is not a measure of the evidence in the observed data. This paper derives critical t-statistics at which the null’s share of the likelihood equals the chosen significance level. The thresholds have a closed form and hold exactly in small samples where the variance must be estimated. At the 5% level the familiar hurdle of |t| ≥ 2 becomes |t| ≥ 2.5. detail.abstract: This paper examines whether machine learning models can serve as effective frameworks for detecting financial market stress. Using daily data on the S&P 500, the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), oil, gold, and the US Dollar Index from January 2006 to September 2026, we construct a binary financial stress indicator and evaluate three classifiers—logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost—trained on the 2006–2022 sample and tested out-of-sample on 2023–2026. The results show that volatility-based indicators dominate the detection signal and that tree-based ensembles capture nonlinear stress–volatility relationships more effectively than the linear benchmark. We discuss the practical implications and limitations of these findings for market surveillance and financial risk monitoring. The evidence suggests that artificial intelligence provides a powerful framework for real-time stress detection, although its performance should be interpreted as market-state identification rather than long-horizon crisis forecasting.​

detail.abstract: Maintaining reliable short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasts over years is difficult because forecast errors evolve on different timescales. Minute-scale weather disturbances require rapid correction, whereas changes in the input--output mapping and seasonal operating conditions require stable long-term adaptation. Repeated site-level diagnosis, retraining, and recalibration create a maintenance burden for distributed PV fleets. We present SCORE, a causal multi-timescale framework that adds self-maintenance to heterogeneous forecasting backbones. SCORE combines a backbone updated monthly, a zero-initialized residual student adapted through five-minute temporal-difference learning and daily replay, a seasonal solar envelope calibrated only on training data, and a bounded residual adapter for persistent bias within the feasible domain. At each event boundary, the framework uses only matured labels and observations available at that boundary to issue immutable forecasts 5, 10, and 15 min ahead. We evaluated SCORE with eight backbones on three co-located PV systems that differ in module technology and rated capacity, using six years of continuous deployment data. Among 24 matched comparisons with monthly updated backbones, SCORE reduced mean absolute error in 23 cases, with improvements ranging from 9.16% to 55.87%. The only exception was PatchTST at Site 3, for which error increased by approximately 0.10%. No forecast was negative, nonzero during a solar-unavailable period, or above the seasonal upper bound. These results show that separating fast and slow adaptation improves long-term forecast reliability while preserving strict temporal information boundaries. The framework provides a practical basis for reducing repeated site-specific retraining across large PV fleets.

detail.title: Experimental evidence on heat pump and retrofit subsidies
detail.abstract: Heat pumps often require complementary building-fabric upgrades to work most efficiently, a requirement that may explain persistent gaps between policy targets and household uptake. Using a nationally representative survey experiment of over 1,000 homeowners with oil or gas heating systems, this paper examines homeowner willingness to switch to a heat pump when faced with building fabric upgrades under different levels of financial support. Retrofit requirements were tailored to dwelling characteristics, while heat pump and retrofit grant levels were independently randomised. Learning about heat pump benefits increased willingness to switch, but this increase was largely eliminated once respondents learned of retrofit requirements of their home. Enhanced grants for both heat pumps and complementary upgrades partially offset this decline. Results further show that grant support influences willingness more strongly than equivalent decreases in private costs. A €1,000 increase in grant support raised willingness by 1.50 points, versus a 0.90-point reduction from an equivalent rise in private retrofit costs, suggesting subsidies carry value beyond their direct financial effect. Resistance to upgrades appears to operate mainly through cost, although homeowners in older dwellings and lower-income households remain less willing to adopt even when costs and grant support are held constant. Meeting heat pump targets under fabric-adequacy policies will likely require substantially greater and better-targeted subsidies, although financial support alone may be insufficient to overcome barriers faced by some households, particularly those living in older homes and with lower incomes.

detail.title: Physical Climate Risk, Tobins’Q and Credit Risk: Evidence from the Oil and Gas Industry
detail.abstract: This paper examines how physical climate risk affects firm valuation and credit risk in the oil and gas industry. Using firm-level data, we find that higher exposure to physical risk is associated with lower Tobin’s Q, particularly among smaller firms and those operating in the upstream segment. These results suggest that market valuation reflects firms’ vulnerability to climate-related physical hazards. However, we do not find evidence that physical climate risk influences credit risk when measured through the Black-Scholes-Merton model. Robustness checks using both relative valuation measures and a restricted credit risk sample excluding zero-probability observations confirm our findings. These results demonstrate that climate vulnerability must be assessed through a highly contextual lens.

detail.abstract: Accurate multi-parameter water quality forecasting is crucial for coastal ecological conservation and mariculture hazard early-warning. However, in-situ observations are severely plagued by prolonged data missingness and strong noise. Furthermore, non-stationary hydrodynamic transport, multiscale temporal aliasing, and cumulative multi-step errors severely hinder long-horizon modeling. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes a Multiscale Frequency-decoupled and Topology-Enhanced Spatiotemporal Graph Convolutional Network (MF-TESGCN). First, masked Tucker tensor decomposition is employed to reliably reconstruct missing observations via global low-rank correlations. Next, a tri-branch embedding module disentangles water quality attributes, dual-scale temporal rhythms, and spatial spectral positions. Spatially, a multi-view dynamic graph generator integrates geometric priors with instantaneous advection–diffusion dynamics to capture time-varying hydrodynamic topologies. Temporally, an orthogonal Fourier transform decomposes signals into trend, periodic, and transient sub-bands, feeding dedicated causal graph convolutions with matched receptive fields. Finally, a mixture-of-experts decoder with dynamic calibration mitigates amplitude decay and baseline drift over long horizons. Extensive experiments on a multi-buoy dataset from the Beibu Gulf, China, show that MF-TESGCN reduces the 24-hour mean squared error (MSE) by 5.61% against the best baseline, while achieving an MAE of 0.2934 and an R2 of 0.8662 in 6-hour forecasts. With merely 80.8K parameters, MF-TESGCN offers an accurate, lightweight solution for operational coastal water quality forecasting.

detail.abstract: As variable renewable generation expands, demand-side flexibility is becoming increasingly important for power-system balancing, yet aggregators must determine day-ahead commitments before operating requirements and resource availability are fully known. This timing mismatch can leave available flexibility underused or increase exposure to adverse delivery outcomes, making risk-aware allocation a central challenge for day-ahead demand-response scheduling. Scenario-based scheduling has improved uncertainty representation and tail-risk control, but treating scenario construction, reduction and probability uncertainty separately can weaken the decision information carried into the final allocation. This study develops a decision-fidelity-aware distributionally robust conditional value-at-risk (DR-CVaR) framework that combines copula-guided historical trajectory matching, decision-loss-guided scenario reduction and a KL ambiguity set. Historical matching retains coherent intraday sequences, decision-loss-guided reduction uses commitment-relevant loss differences to retain trajectories that shape hourly allocation, and DR-CVaR protects the resulting allocation against plausible probability shifts and tail losses. Validation shows that the compact representation improves joint-state fidelity and preserves full-library commitment behaviour. Across 360 held-out operating days, DR-CVaR achieved 76.4% flexible-resource utilisation, reduced unused response-envelope capacity by 15.4–39.2%, and retained the lowest mean and tail common-KL composite model-loss scores among four matched strategies. The additional model-estimated response was allocated to peak-load windows in all four seasons, lowering mean peak equivalent load by 35.8–139.0 MW relative to the three comparator strategies and showing that more effective flexibility utilisation strengthens peak-load support under probability and tail-risk stress.

detail.abstract: This study provides an integrative analysis of the implementation, acceptability, and operational dynamics of Ecuador's School Feeding Program in rural Andean contexts. By examining key stakeholders' perspectives, it offers evidence-based insights into the structural and nutritional challenges of school meal provision. To explore the perceptions, experiences, and barriers related to school breakfast served in public schools among children and teachers in rural Andean communities in the province of Chimborazo, Ecuador, an exploratory qualitative study was conducted based on in-depth, semi-structured interviews with students and teachers involved in the Umiña Project. Data were analysed inductively using thematic analysis until data saturation was reached, and the findings were subsequently organized according to a SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) framework, with inter-rater reliability showing high agreement (Kappa = 0.89). A total of thirty-two students and ten teachers participated in the study. The findings revealed significant weaknesses associated with the low sensory acceptability of the products distributed by the state program, which were frequently described by students as having a monotonous taste, unpleasant texture, or unattractive appearance. Conversely, among the strengths, teachers highlighted the logistical continuity of the government program, the universal coverage of the rations, and the institutional organization for their daily distribution. Ultimately, Ecuador's School Feeding Program demonstrates adequate coverage and operational continuity; however, its nutritional impact remains limited by the low sensory acceptability of the food, the limited cultural relevance of the menus, and a food environment characterized by the widespread availability of ultra-processed products.

In this paper, a novel machine learning framework for reconstruction and temporal prediction in case of missing data in an IoT-enabled xEV-integrated DC microgrid consisting of solar PV, wind generation, battery energy storage, and xEV systems is presented. title: Reliability―Aware Evidential Fusion with Information-Bottleneck Guarantees for Robust Multimodal Learning under Missing and Corrupted Modalities
affiliations: Anyang Normal University

detail.title: Reliability―Aware Evidential Fusion with Information-Bottleneck Guarantees for Robust Multimodal Learning under Missing and Corrupted Modalities
detail.abstract: Multimodal recognition systems routinely operate under incomplete and degraded sensor streams: modalities are absent at test time, individual sensors fail silently, and surviving sensors may disagree with one another. Existing fusion heuristics conflate these failure modes into a single uncertainty scalar, weight modalities by learned gates whose behavior under shifted sensors is undocumented, and rarely state conditions under which fusion cannot hurt the best surviving sensor. We propose Reliability-Aware Evidential Fusion (RAEF), a framework that (i) decomposes each modality's reliability into epistemic vacuity, aleatoric spread, and cross-modal conflict before any discounting is applied; (ii) combines reliability-discounted Dirichlet opinions with the reliability-discounted logarithmic opinion pooling with residual dissonance gating (RDF-LGP) operator, which pools log-evidence, routes residual dissonance into enlarged fused uncertainty rather than averaging it away, and restores confidence only when independent sensors agree; and (iii) optimizes a cross-modal information bottleneck (CMIB) that suppresses nuisance sharing while preserving label sufficiency. We prove a reliability-weighted fusion risk bound and a no-harm condition, with an O(ξ) concentration corollary. On a controlled three-modality benchmark with real training runs across five seeds, RAEF reaches 98.7% clean accuracy, holds expected calibration error at 11.9% under isolated-sensor corruption against 35.1% for dynamic evidential fusion, raises out-of-distribution AUROC to 85.4, and remains flat at 98.7% through 80% missingness. Calibrated tables on AVMNIST, NYUDv2, CREMA-D, and Houston2013 reproduce the same ordering, reducing mean corruption error from 29.6 to 23.2.

detail.abstract: We examine how Chinese equity markets price firm-level trade exposure across 3 sequential U.S.–China tariff escalations of widening scope: a targeted episode in March 2018, a broad episode in May 2019, and a systemic episode in April 2025. Using a sequential event-study design and a panel of 186 A-share firms classified by product-level tariff targeting, U.S. revenue exposure, and state ownership, we find that direct targeting and U.S. revenue dependence are associated with large negative abnormal returns primarily during the targeted episode, whereas the broad episode generates an economy-wide decline in which exposure-based differentiation largely disappears. During the systemic episode, exposure pricing re-emerges sharply on the impact day, yet the explicit equity backstop provided by Central Huijin and the subsequent U.S. exemption of electronics compress cumulative losses within days. Peak-day responses intensify monotonically with escalation scope, while 10-day cumulative responses do not. A discount on privately owned enterprises emerges from the second episode onward, consistent with investors learning that implicit state support is unevenly distributed. The evidence indicates that exposure-based pricing is episode-dependent and conditioned by the evolving policy backstop, although the controls employed cannot fully separate learning from institutional change

detail.abstract: This paper presents an exploratory, multi-factor model for assessing global ecological and socioeconomic collapse risk. A hand-computed five-factor weighted index, supported by descriptive statistics, a rate equation, an impact-matrix eigenvalue analysis, a linear program and classical hypothesis tests (t-test, χ 2 , one-way ANOVA, Tukey HSD), is first documented and verified with software. The model is then extended to eight factors by adding biodiversity, conflict and resource indicators compiled from published global statistics, and a multilayer-perceptron (MLP) surrogate with Monte-Carlo simulation is used to propagate uncertainty to 2100. The five-factor index is 69.65% and the eight-factor index is 64.30% (MLP: 64.31%, R 2 = 0.959). The dominant eigenvalue of the 8×8 impact matrix is λ max = 1.563 (> 1), indicating self-reinforcing coupling under the assumed couplings. Interstellar escape probability, estimated as 120/73,000 = 0.16%, shows that no practical alternative to Earth exists with current technology. In scenario analysis, raising net recovery capacity from 0.35 to 1.0 index-points per year reduces the probability of crossing a critical level (75) before 2100 from 89% to 14%. Weights, thresholds and couplings are author-assigned; results are therefore illustrative and not a forecast.

title: Childcare Waitlists
affiliations: London Business School, University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business and University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School - Operations, Information and Decisions

detail.title: Childcare Waitlists

affiliations.org_name: University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - Stephen M. Ross School of Business
University of Pennsylvania - Operations & Information Management Department

detail.abstract:
Parents seeking childcare often face long waitlists. At the same time, vacancies at childcare centers can remain unfilled for extended periods. We trace this paradox to two persistent features of childcare services. First, families consider multiple child care options due to enrollment uncertainties, resulting in phantom listings that remain on waitlists even after families have found care elsewhere or no longer need a slot. Second, filling a slot is time-consuming: centers learn whether a family is actively seeking enrollment only after making an offer and waiting for a response. As families pursue alternatives while they wait and their children age, these delays and feedback effects amplify the mismatch between demand and available capacity. 

We study two operational remedies. First, we examine regular verification that removes phantom listings before offers are made, improving the efficiency of enrollment and reducing vacancies. Second, we study mixed-age classrooms, in which some slots designated for older children can be flexibly used by younger children. This flexibility increases utilization, shortens waits, and reduces wasted offers. Its benefits extend beyond conventional pooling: as children move between age groups, classrooms can be filled through internal flows rather than costly external search, further reducing enrollment delays. Together, verification and mixed use offer a way to expand effective capacity in early childhood classrooms, where regulatory and operational constraints make adding physical capacity particularly costly.

title: Grid-based Gibbs-energy initialization of near-critical three-phase CO2–hydrocarbon flash calculations
affiliations: Moscow State University

detail.title: Grid-based Gibbs-energy initialization of near-critical three-phase CO2–hydrocarbon flash calculations
detail.abstract: Three-phase liquid–liquid–vapour (L1–L2–V) flash calculations can be difficult to initialize near the critical region, where an incipient phase may occupy a narrow part of composition space. We evaluate a grid-based Gibbs-energy initializer against stability-directed sequential phase addition for CO2–hydrocarbon systems. The grid method minimizes Gibbs energy by linear programming over a discretized composition simplex. Candidate phase counts and compositions are then refined by successive substitution and screened using a multistart tangent-plane-distance test. In a prespecified 486-state benchmark, both initializers used the same refinement algorithm, stability criterion, and acceptance rules; the sequential baseline was given a larger stability-search budget. The grid initializer recovered 15 thermodynamically verified three-phase states located by either approach, compared with 10 for sequential phase addition, and recovered more states at every tested grid resolution. For the five states recovered only by the grid method, independent dense scans indicated that the two-phase solutions were unstable and that the incipient phases were localized near a simplex edge, at heavy-component mole fractions of order 10−4. Adding edge-focused trial compositions to the stability search recovered all 15 states without grid initialization. At 294 K, the ordering reversed: sequential addition recovered 47 of 48 states, compared with 39 for the grid method. The workflow was also validated against published transition pressures and compositions. These results indicate that grid-based initialization can improve recovery in the specific near-critical, edge-localized regime examined, while boundary-focused stability searches offer an alternative.

detail.abstract: Organisations are beginning to use AI to generate financial reports, yet human reviewers may over-trust algorithmic output (automation bias), and review effort is often applied uniformly regardless of the quality of the underlying data or the consequences of an error. This paper reviews literature on data governance, data quality management, human-in-the-loop oversight and automation bias, and identifies a gap: within the sources reviewed, little work links the intensity of human review to both data quality and the impact of error. It proposes a conceptual three-tier review framework that assigns oversight using a data-quality score and an impact classification, with an impact floor for high-stakes outputs, random spot checks of the lightest tier, dynamic tier reassignment, and periodic validation of the quality scoring itself. The framework is a proposal and has not been empirically tested. The sources come mainly from data governance, information systems and human-AI interaction research, and several relate to financial reporting only by analogy. The paper contributes a structured way to discuss proportionate oversight of AI-generated reports and a set of questions for future empirical work. It also sets out the framework's limitations, including its dependence on the reliability of the quality scoring, and the evidence needed to evaluate it.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether regulatory inquiry letters curb corporate artificial intelligence (AI) washing. Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2015 to 2024, we find that firms receiving inquiry letters exhibit significantly lower AI washing driven mainly by less AI-related disclosure. Mechanism tests show that regulatory inquiries reduce upward earnings management and managerial tone manipulation, suggesting that they constrain managers’ opportunistic reporting. The effect is stronger when inquiry letters are more detailed, firms provide more extensive responses, and intermediaries are required to issue professional opinions. It is also stronger among financially distressed firms and in regions with stronger legal institutions. These findings show that external monitoring is more effective when scrutiny is sufficiently strong, firms are required to respond, and disclosed information can be verified.

detail.abstract: Digital labor platforms use algorithms not only to assign, monitor, and compensate workers, but also to shape how tasks are performed. We study a bundle-level picking timer that shows workers an estimate of expected grocery-picking time. The estimate is purely informational: beating or missing it has no effect on pay, ratings, or future work allocation. Yet faster picking may reflect genuine efficiency gains, such as better pacing and organized search, or effort displacement, such as less persistent search and earlier abandonment of hard-to-find items, with implications for service quality. Using a randomized field experiment spanning more than two years and covering tens of millions of bundle-level tasks performed by more than 200,000 workers across a large retail store network, we estimate the causal effect of timer access on picking time and refunds. On average, the timer makes workers 2.8% faster but raises refunds by 0.77%, suggesting that some speed gains may come at the expense of quality. This average masks substantial heterogeneity. Speed gains are larger for bigger baskets, early in a worker's workday, and on weekends. In operating environments that may proxy for greater task difficulty, the timer continues to reduce picking time while its adverse effect on refunds is attenuated, creating a more favorable speed-quality tradeoff. The effect is also concentrated among gig workers and essentially absent among permanent employees, whose routines and store familiarity may provide an internal pacing benchmark. These findings show that algorithmic timing can serve as a strategic managerial lever for balancing efficiency and service quality.

detail.abstract: Improving the coordinated operation of energy and water resources is essential for agricultural parks. However, short-term source-load prediction errors are considerable, which often forces uncertainty-based optimization methods to be overly conservative. Moreover, demand-side flexible resources remain underexploited. To tackle these problems, this paper proposes a two-stage distributionally robust optimization (DRO) scheduling strategy. The strategy integrates two key components: an improved incentive-based integrated demand response (IBIDR) covering electricity, heat, and water, and a data-driven ellipsoidal uncertainty set constructed from CNN-Transformer-MTL prediction errors. The main work is threefold. First, a CNN-Transformer-MTL prediction model is developed to improve the prediction accuracy of PV power and heat load. An ellipsoidal uncertainty set is then constructed based on the prediction errors, which significantly reduces the conservativeness of the set. Second, the improved IBIDR is designed for electricity, heat, and water loads. It combines stepped subsidies for adjustable loads with substitution-based response of replaceable loads. Third, four models are compared: a deterministic model, a DRO model without demand response, a DRO model with price-based integrated demand response, and the proposed improved IBIDR-DRO model. Case study results are as follows. The CNN-Transformer-MTL model achieves the best prediction performance for both PV power and heat load. The resulting uncertainty set has the smallest area: it is up to 24.64% smaller than those built from the errors of other prediction models, and 27.3% smaller than the box set at the same confidence level. This effectively alleviates the over-conservatism of DRO. Meanwhile, the proposed model reduces the total operating cost by 10.4% compared with the DRO model, and by 7.1% compared with the DRO model with price-based integrated demand response. In particular, the flexible scheduling of pumps and water storage facilities cuts the peak pump load by 23%, confirming the role of the water subsystem as a flexibility provider. These results demonstrate that integrating data-driven uncertainty characterization with incentive-based demand response is an effective way to unlock the flexibility of energy-water nexus systems.

detail.abstract: Measuring anticompetitive effects can improve merger decisions even when transaction-specific efficiencies are uncertain or can be measured imprecisely only. Metcalfe, Sollaci and Syverson (2026) have shown that privately viable mergers producing significant market power effects yield lower expected efficiencies. This paper shows that, when private viability is accounted for, merger control agencies should expect higher efficiencies for a given level of harm and, therefore, op-timally adapt their clearance thresholds to reduce the likelihood of Type 1 errors (erroneous prohibitions). Furthermore, we show that the expected level of efficiencies for a given level of harm and the optimal clearance threshold both increase with the costs of merger completion, filing and review. Therefore, measuring harm leads to merger decisions that better reflect potential efficiencies, even when they are unobserved, and are less likely to give rise to Type 1 errors without hurting consumers due to the ensuing increase in Type 2 errors (erroneous clearances). A merger control policy that renounces to measure harm and contents itself with identifying the possibility of harm is thus consumer welfare detrimental.

title: AI for Managing Agile Projects: From Assistant to AI Software Factory
